content.text:
I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral table, and all six figure briefs, and built a full source ledger before deciding.

**Ledger highlights (all traced):**

- **Claims 1–10 (device):** rigid base with first/second sides, motor on the first side, extraction mechanism on the first side in fluid communication with a second-side chamber, rigid low-friction perimeter loop, non-sealing clearance admitting ambient air, sustained sub-atmospheric chamber, operator-free holding force, sliding while held, materials list (plastic/metal/PTFE/combinations), vacuum pump, handle for guiding — all trace to the disclosure's own sentences. Claim 10's stirring elements and "constant forward motion" trace to the USER passage "we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion."
- **Claims 11–15 (system) and 16–20 (method):** the pulling element (rope/wire/cable), decoupled position-vs-hold control, continuous maintenance during translation, and PTFE all trace to the disclosure's final paragraph and the perimeter-material sentence.
- **Numerals 10–48:** each maps to exactly one part, appears in at least one brief, and every numeral cited in the description appears on the figure cited there.
- **Figure briefs:** section designations 2-2 and 4-4 are used identically in the FIG. 3 source view, the FIG. 2/FIG. 4 view lines, and the Brief Description. Horizontal line 2-2 cuts the loop twice → FIG. 2's two legs; vertical line 4-4 → FIG. 4's single fragmentary column. Consistent.
- **Depiction conventions stay inside the briefs.** The slab/band/ring/column outlines, the block order in FIG. 1, the schematic gap through the base in FIG. 2, the flat lower end in FIG. 4, and the number/placement of the FIG. 6 stirring elements are each disclaimed within their own brief. The application text uses only "shown schematically" / "shown enlarged for clarity" — no "by way of example," no "any closed outline," no embodiment broadened to justify a renderer choice. No brief verbalizes taper, angle, runout, relative depth, or end position for the bearing face, clearance, or port.
- **Text checks:** no drafting note, placeholder, question, instruction, or unresolved alternative in any draft section; the Background's "second problem" now has its "first of two problems" antecedent; the FIG. 2 Brief Description enumeration matches the FIG. 2 brief's cut bodies; the prior-art "sliding base" is consistently qualified so the bare noun stays reserved for base 12.

Nothing untraced or inconsistent surfaced, so the findings array is empty.

input.summary: Full source-fidelity preflight completed against input/disclosure.md and the affirmative USER passages in input/conversation.md, with input/brief.md used only for title, applicant, inventor, priority and government-support formalities. Every limitation of all twenty claims (device claims 1-10, system claims 11-15, method claims 16-20) was traced to an exact affirmative inventor passage: the rigid base with first and second sides, the vibration motor coupled to the first side, the air-extraction mechanism coupled to the first side and in fluid communication with the second-side chamber, the rigid low-friction perimeter loop or skirt, the non-sealing clearance through which ambient air continuously enters, the volumetric extraction rate maintaining the chamber below atmospheric pressure, the operator-free holding force from the pressure differential, the all-rigid vibration path with no elastomeric, foam or resilient member interposed, sliding to successive areas while the hold is maintained, the plastic/metal/PTFE/combination material list, the vacuum pump, the guiding handle, and the rope, wire or cable flexible pulling element with decoupled position-versus-hold control. The stirring elements, autonomous constant forward motion and the "need not be pulled or guided by hand" recitals in claim 10, the Summary, the Field and the FIG. 6 material trace to the USER passage adding an autonomous mode with small stirring elements. All seventeen numerals (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48) were checked: each denotes exactly one part, each appears on at least one sheet, each brief's numeral list matches the numerals its geometry text uses, and every "as shown in FIG. n" cross-reference in the detailed description names a figure whose brief actually carries that numeral. All six figure briefs and the Brief Description of the Drawings were compared line by line: the FIG. 2 enumeration of sectioned bodies matches the FIG. 2 brief's hatched slab, legs and covering-element band with the air-extraction housing in elevation; section line 2-2 carries the same repeated designation in the FIG. 3 source view, the FIG. 2 view line and the drawing description, and section line 4-4 likewise in FIG. 3, FIG. 4 and the drawing description; the horizontal 2-2 cut of the ring yields the two legs drawn in FIG. 2 and the vertical 4-4 cut yields the single fragmentary column of FIG. 4. Depiction conventions were tested under the functional-surface rule: the slab, band, ring, column and block outlines, the block order in FIG. 1, the schematic passage from the housing to the chamber in FIG. 2, the flat lower end of the perimeter member in FIG. 4, and the number, form and placement of the FIG. 6 stirring elements are each disclaimed inside their own brief only, and none verbalizes taper, angle, runout direction, relative depth, radial or circumferential end position, or contact topology beyond the affirmatively disclosed rigid contact and the disclosed clearance beneath the rigid perimeter. No convention leaks into the application text: the specification and Brief Description use only "shown schematically" and "shown enlarged for clarity", with no "by way of example", no "any closed outline", and no optional embodiment added to justify a renderer's visual choice. Internal text review found claims and description using the same terms and relationships, prior-art "sliding base" consistently qualified so the bare noun stays reserved for base 12, the Background's "second problem" sentence supplied with its "first of two problems" antecedent, correct claim dependencies and antecedent basis, and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction to a person, unresolved alternative or internal comment anywhere in the ten draft sections or the six briefs. Prior-art characterizations in the Background were left to the later citation review as directed. No untraced structure, relationship, result, material, shape, position, connection, operating condition or variant was found, and no verified internal inconsistency remains, so the findings array is empty.
